clue.text: Checks what's on the floor

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to carpet someone is to reprimand them, so it is a verb, checks
second meaning: rugs and floor coverings

explanation.surface: Someone inspecting the flooring, or a pattern of squares on the rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' suggests a chequered pattern on a rug; here it is the verb meaning reprimands, as in being 'carpeted' by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet is an informal British verb for to reprimand, and carpets are also the woven coverings laid over floors.

clue.text: One in tree where races can be watched

parts.note: a means one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spectator perched up a tree to get a view of the races.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the racecourse near Liverpool that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous English horse-racing venue, a place for watching races.

clue.text: Sang shrilly, giving editor the pip

parts.note: taken as written
ed is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A singer's screeching annoyed the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving someone the pip' is a British idiom for annoying them.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe is to sing or speak in a high, thin voice, so piped means trilled shrilly.

clue.text: Round fat cheese kept in fabric

indicators.note: turning something round sends it back the other way

parts.note: taken as written
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A round, fatty cheese wrapped in cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round fat cheese' looks like a description of a wheel of cheese; 'Round' turns the next word back.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven silk material, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Reversing motorists about to get a fool's remains

indicators.note: something reversing goes backwards, so the motoring club's letters are read from the end

parts.note: the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motoring organisation
c, short for circa, means about
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Drivers backing up and ending up with the dead body of an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The motoring club here is the British breakdown service; 'remains' at the end is the definition, not a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcass is the dead body of an animal, what remains after death.

clue.text: Relaxed in the sea tho' meditating

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: Someone meditating by the sea, although relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'sea' through 'tho'' into 'meditating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at home in a situation means feeling comfortable and at ease.

clue.text: It being most bitter in Paris, she is wearing a coat

indicators.note: someone wearing a garment is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a crust is an outer coat or layer
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A woman in Paris wrapped in a coat because it is bitterly cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most bitter' suggests the weather, but here it means most harsh in temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruellest means most harsh and unkind, matching bitter in the sense of savage.

clue.text: Crushes a relative

wordplay.note: read as a two-word phrasal verb meaning treads on underfoot, then written as one word

explanation.surface: Someone stamping on a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Crushes' as the phrase steps on, then run the two words together.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is the son of one's spouse from a previous partnership, a family relation.

clue.text: Exotic fern with mud and starch found on the table

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd table decoration made of plants, mud and starch.
explanation.walkthrough: All three words together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: French mustard is a mild condiment commonly set out at the dining table.

clue.text: Sleep after a second in this card game

indicators.note: after sets the order: the sleep word is placed second, behind the second

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone dozing off a moment into a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep after a second' tells you NAP comes after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a simple children's card game in which players shout when two matching cards appear.

clue.text: Remote rodent's going round hospital buildings

parts.note: remote means far away

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent; the 's is read as 'is', giving MOUSE plus S
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A distant mouse scurrying around the hospital's buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'rodent's' is read as 'is', supplying the plural S, and the hospital letter slips in just after the first letter of the rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmhouses are the dwellings on farms, a kind of building.

clue.text: Woman in white traditionally keeps good connection

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a bride traditionally wears a white dress
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A bride in a white gown holding on to a good relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge is a structure that connects two places, so it is a link or connection.

clue.text: Unlabelled in men's sale, maybe

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters could be arranged some other way

parts.note: the letters of these two words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Unbranded goods turning up in a menswear sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nameless has no name attached, so it is without a label.

clue.text: Complain whiningly, making corporation suffer

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a large paunch
to ache is to suffer pain

explanation.surface: Someone moaning about a company being made to struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but it is the dated humorous word for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellyache is an informal idiom meaning to grumble or whinge persistently.

clue.text: Deploring repair of mangle with tin

indicators.note: a repair puts things back together, here in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Regretting fixing an old clothes mangle with a bit of tin.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangle is an old wringer with rollers for squeezing water out of washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamenting means expressing sorrow or regret over something, much as deploring does.

clue.text: Party treat: a bone!

indicators.note: to treat something is to process or work on it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A dog's party treat: a bone!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party treat' reads as a single phrase, but 'Party' is the definition and 'treat' the anagram signal. A beano is British slang for a lively celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is informal British slang for a festive gathering or knees-up.

clue.text: Large prawns, not quite enough for cheeky child

indicators.note: not quite enough means falling a little short, so the end is cut off

parts.note: scampi are large prawns, Dublin Bay prawns

explanation.surface: A greedy child complaining the plate of prawns is too small.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAMPI loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous young rascal, an impudent child.

clue.text: Shut down street that is most friendly

parts.note: to close is to shut down
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A road that has been closed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Close friends are intimate ones, so the closest are the most intimate.

clue.text: Ernie endlessly coming outside for movables

indicators.note: coming outside means wrapping around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: coming, as an adjective, means future

indicators.note: without its ends means both the first and last letters go, leaving the middle

parts.note: the name with its ends removed

explanation.surface: Ernie arriving outside, endlessly, with the household goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming' looks like a verb about Ernie, but it is the adjective future, which goes around RNI.
explanation.definitionFit: Movables is a legal term for property that can be moved, such as tables and chairs, i.e. furniture.

clue.text: Barely visible

parts.note: surface reading: only just able to be seen
setter's reading: in a bare state, i.e. without clothes, and visible like that

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' looks like 'hardly', but it is the adverb from bare, unclothed.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer describes being seen in the nude, which is what barely, in its unclothed sense, means.

clue.text: Staggering round, having eaten fish

indicators.note: something that has eaten another thing holds it inside

parts.note: a ring is round
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone tottering about after a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeling means lurching unsteadily, as a person does when dizzy or drunk.

clue.text: Old girl needs help when embraced by men

indicators.note: something embraced is held within arms, so it sits inside

parts.note: taken as written
aid is help

explanation.surface: An elderly woman needing assistance from some men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old girl' looks like an elderly woman; here it means a girl in old-fashioned language.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden is an archaic or literary word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Depressed by sad actors

parts.note: feeling down is feeling sad
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: Someone dispirited by a gloomy troupe of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast is a synonym for dejected, low in spirits.

clue.text: Struck, being abandoned

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hit with the foot
second meaning: given up, as a habit is

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the idiom of kicking a habit, meaning giving it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicked means hit with a foot, and in the idiom 'kicked the habit' it means gave up or quit.

clue.text: Island's star goat is short of corn

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Capricorn is the star sign of the goat
taken as written; this is what is removed

explanation.surface: A celebrated goat on an island running out of feed.
explanation.walkthrough: Capricorn, the goat of the zodiac, loses CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Confused English film director found in bed

indicators.note: found in tells us these pieces sit inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written; it is split around the rest
E is the abbreviation for English
Billy Wilder, director of Some Like It Hot

explanation.surface: An English film-maker discovered in bed, presumably baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Wilder was the Hollywood director of Some Like It Hot and The Apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewildered is a synonym for perplexed or utterly puzzled.

clue.text: A couple's quiet manner

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: Describing a couple who carry themselves in a calm way.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two of something, the same as a couple.

clue.text: Presenting silver in swindle

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Handing over silverware as part of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Staging a play is putting it on, presenting it to an audience.

clue.text: It helps medically to burn your inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: to singe is to burn lightly
yr is the abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: A medicine that works by burning inside you.
explanation.definitionFit: A syringe is a medical device for injecting or drawing fluids, a tool used in treatment.
